reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Same AI, separate source-first pass after drafting. Reread Articles 3.1, 3.3 and 3.5 and Annexes 1–3 to reconstruct the 127.5 EC major and 52.5 EC profiling from the formal rules, and compared those requirements with the 2026 cohort sequence and programme course descriptions. Rechecked the primary degree and prospectus pages for interest scope, language and the distinction between literature, culture and language proficiency. Reconsidered UCR course contributions and the limits of direct row pairing against the current workbook, then checked the frozen and replayed record and the fields and selected descriptions used by the renderer.
findings: The standard Utrecht Spanish Language and Culture degree totals 180 EC. Article 3.5 and Annexes 1–2 establish a 127.5 EC major: 67.5 EC of compulsory courses, 7.5 EC for the Spanish-language thesis, 45 EC of advanced courses and one 7.5 EC methods course. Annex 3 establishes 52.5 EC of profiling, including a 30 EC coherent package. A Utrecht minor qualifies; an external minor, study abroad or a specially assembled package needs advance approval. The Crossing Borders depth package may also serve as profiling in this track. The Crossing Borders track has a different major and profiling division. The prospectus describes subject matter and provides learning context; the OER and start-year guide control the selected requirements. The degree is mainly in Spanish with some English courses under Article 3.3. The 0 EC basic grammar test is required, and the programme outcomes include at least B2 speaking and writing and C1 listening and reading.

The illustrated Year 1 follows the two required base packages and the A1 to B2 Spanish acquisition sequence alongside literary studies, comparative morphosyntax, theater and film, and sociolinguistics. In 2027–2028, the odd rotation places literacy and cultural awareness, Migration and Diaspora, Testimonios, crónicas, representaciones, and Variation and Change in Language in successive blocks. Formal titles and credit values control; the prospectus currently uses imágenes in its title for the testimony and chronicles course. The four odd-year catalog codes were pending in the OER. The chosen level-3 intercultural communication methods course fits block 3 alongside that block’s depth course. Profiling fills the remaining 22.5 EC in Year 2. In 2028–2029, the first two advanced courses in the even rotation fit blocks 1 and 2. The writing workshop and thesis run in blocks 3 and 4 respectively in the cohort guide. The six depth courses, methods, writing and thesis yield 67.5 EC at level 3, above the 45 EC minimum. The 30 EC coherent package fills the remaining Year 3 load.

The closest plan builds from historical and literary foundations to the study of empire, Indigenous resistance, heritage, migration and representations of the past. Renaissance Italy and the Global Mediterranean contributes cross-cultural art and colonial trade. Native American Histories and the advanced history seminar contribute historical interpretation and source-based independent research. Modern Art and Modern Museums includes Mexican muralism, a specific example of Latin American content within a wider curriculum. Roman and Arab Spain, the Franco dictatorship and the Spanish conquest are grounded comparator interests. The UCR history and heritage courses give relevant comparative context, with no dedicated Spanish or Latin American historical sequence implied. The second plan combines stylistics, rhetoric and literary interpretation with gender history, race, environmental media, community speaking and documentary. Environmental media and persuasion share a concrete thematic thread from analyzing representation to designing messages, while gender history contributes a primary-source account of identity. The current workbook search covered language acquisition, Spanish, Hispanic, translation, sociolinguistics, morphology, film, media, migration, colonial history and region-specific topics using available descriptions as well as structured fields. It supplies relevant general stylistics, psycholinguistics and cultural analysis. It lacks an active Spanish proficiency sequence or enough Spanish-specific advanced linguistics and writing for a third eligible direction. Direct alignments are limited to literary analysis, adaptation across media, and contested histories. Migration, qualitative methods, stylistics and life writing have broader or different objects of study and are shown separately with scope notes. The 7.5 EC Utrecht thesis remains required; the optional 15 EC UCR research comparison element remains outside the degree schedule.
